data.title: Trump to Announce Medicaid Drug Pricing After Pharma Deals — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Catherine Dunn

President Donald Trump is set to announce on Friday the participation of all states in a Medicaid drug pricing model that follows deals struck with 17 major pharmaceutical companies over the past year.

The announcement builds on the president's push to get drug manufacturers to agree to lower prescription drug prices in the U.S. to price levels in other countries that typically pay less-a concept dubbed most favored nation, or MFN.

Full details of the agreements haven't been publicly released. The pricing provisions generally apply to future product launches, as well as to existing drugs purchased within the Medicaid program, the joint federal-state insurance program that covers people with lower income.

Drug companies had incentives to participate in the deals to stave off the threat of U.S. tariffs on their products. Wall Street generally reacted well to the MFN deals as they were released, starting with Pfizer in September 2025, as a cloud of uncertainty lifted.

The NYSE Arca Pharmaceutical Index was down about 0.50% in early afternoon trading, slightly lower than the broader market, which was down about 0.20%.

In a Friday morning client note, Mizuho's Jared Holz said the health of large-cap pharma companies "has improved markedly over the past 12-18 months, much of this due to drug pricing agreements and greater certainty around the political climate."

While these big players do face some financial pressure from MFN, as well as the implementation of the Medicare drug pricing provisions in the Biden-era Inflation Reduction Act, "the fact that the there is now more certainty regarding various politically driven tactics allows Companies to strategize and plan more effectively," Holz wrote.

News of today's Medicaid-focused announcement was reported earlier by Semafor and The Hill. A White House spokesperson confirmed to Barron's that all 50 states, D.C., and Puerto Rico will take part in the pricing model known as GENEROUS.

"A key component of the President's MFN deals was for drugmakers to provide drugs at MFN prices immediately to Medicaid, and today's announcement confirms that every state Medicaid program will save billions on prescription drug costs thanks to President Trump," the spokesperson said.

data.title: Global Bond Yields Rise Amid Expectations of More Rate Rises — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Miriam Mukuru and Emese Bartha

Global bond yields rose on Friday, hovering near multiyear highs, after the Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan raised interest rates this week, with more increases expected to come.

The Fed raised interest rates by a quarter point on Wednesday, and signaled another raise to come this year, which convinced markets about the seriousness of the Fed's inflation fight.

This initially pulled yields away from recent highs. However, the factors that drove bond yields higher in the first place remained, namely the risk of oil prices staying elevated for a prolonged period, high debt levels, and competition for funding from AI-related companies.

"The Fed may have reinforced its inflation-fighting credentials, but heavy government borrowing, elevated term premium and growing private-sector competition for capital mean long yields remain supported by forces that monetary policy alone cannot easily resolve," said Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com.

The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield rose back to the 5% level reached earlier this week for the first time since 2023. It was recently at 5.002%. The two-year yield, which tracks Fed moves more closely, touched 4.744%, its highest intraday yield since July 2024 when it hit 4.775%.

Yield moves have mirrored oil prices in recent weeks, but the trend broke on Friday, as Brent fell 1% to $104 a barrel.

Following a Bank of England's hold on Thursday, the Bank of Japan raised its policy rate to 1.25% on Friday, the highest since 1995, albeit in a split vote.

The 10-year Japanese government bond yield was steady at 2.998% after the BOJ decision. With two board members voting against the rate increase, the move wasn't enough to boost the yen, which weakened nearly 1% against the dollar.

Analysts warned that global yields could still rise further.

"The global rebuilding of term premia is not yet complete, and markets still have scope to price a more aggressive path of central bank rate hikes," Societe Generale rates strategists said in a note.

The 10-year German Bund yield rose 2.0 basis points to 3.500%, below a peak of 3.572% hit earlier this week, its highest since 2009. The 10-year U.K. gilt yield climbed 5.7 bps to 5.275%, below this week's peak of 5.493%, its highest since 2007.

Central bank leaders acknowledged the rising inflation risks and signaled more rate rises in the coming months, causing markets to price in three or more rate increases by major central banks in the next year, LSEG data showed.

"The medicine from the Fed is working and may have prevented the rates selloff from spiraling out of control," said Commerzbank rates strategist Marco Stoeckle in a note.

Gilt yields were also lifted after Friday's U.K. retail sales data for August came in better than expected, suggesting that household spending stayed resilient despite high energy costs and increased prospects of higher interest rates by the Bank of England in the future.

  • Paulo Trevisani contributed to this article.

Write to Miriam Mukuru at miriam.mukuru@wsj.com and Emese Bartha at emese.bartha@wsj.com

data.title: Polymarket and Yahoo Finance Partnership Expires
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Polymarket and Yahoo Finance's partnership has ended.

The agreement, which allowed the financial-news platform to showcase Polymarket's prediction-market data on its site, came to the end of its six-month term this spring, a person familiar with the matter said. The deal's terms ended mutually, the person said.

Polymarket announced the exclusive partnership on X in November 2025. Polymarket continues to be an advertising partner with Yahoo.

Polymarket, one of the leading prediction markets providers, has a data partnership with Dow Jones, the publisher of the Wall Street Journal. Rival Kalshi has partnerships with CNN, CNBC and Fox.

The deals are mostly to provide data on how prediction markets users are trading on the outcomes of different events. News outlets showcase different markets to give their audience a sense of how likely traders think it is that an event will occur.

Many advocates for predication markets see this kind of data sharing as one of the most important services the industry can offer, as the information creates insights that can influence decision making. This contrasts with critics of the industry, who say prediction markets are a form of betting that fuel unhealthy financial behaviors among users.

Both Polymarket and Kalshi have their own newsletters with a combination of news and aligning prediction markets data.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: AT&T and Dallas Cowboys Extend One of Sports' Most Iconic Partnerships
data.description:
AT&T's network connects America's Team to what's next in sports and entertainment at AT&T Stadium

Key Takeaways:

  • AT&T and the Dallas Cowboys extend their partnership to power the next generation of technology, experiences and innovation at AT&T Stadium.
  • AT&T is debuting new stadium technology at AT&T Stadium for the 2026 season, powered by the nation's largest fiber1 network, from AI-powered moments and smarter navigation to more immersive fan experiences.

DALLAS, Sept. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AT&T and the Dallas Cowboys today announced an agreement to build the future of sports and entertainment at AT&T Stadium, with AT&T's network continuing to power the infrastructure, technology and in-stadium moments that make the stadium one of the most connected venues in sports and entertainment.

The announcement comes as AT&T and the Cowboys kick off the 2026 season with new fan experiences and technology, from smarter stadium navigation to immersive video, mixed reality and AI-powered moments built for connected fans.

"There is no more critical partner that we rely upon and value than AT&T," said Dallas Cowboys Owner, President and General Manager Jerry Jones. "AT&T is not only at the core of our fan experience and engagement ability, but they provide the foundation of technology and connectivity that drives everything we do operationally. Being able to trust and depend on that like we have for 30 years, and now, knowing we will grow and continue to innovate, is as important a part of our future as anything could be."

Engineering the Connected World of Sports and Entertainment

A satellite signal may reach a stadium, but it takes fiber throughout the venue to deliver the world-class experience fans increasingly expect. When more than 100,000 people gather in one place, connectivity gets put to the test. At AT&T Stadium, more than 261 miles of fiber and nearly 1,000 antennas throughout the venue, the largest network of its kind in the country, help power everything from mobile ticketing and stadium operations to video sharing and real-time fan experiences, engineering the connected world of the biggest stages in sports and entertainment.

The agreement builds on that foundation, giving AT&T and the Dallas Cowboys a platform to create faster, smarter and more immersive ways for fans to experience every moment of game day. The partnership also keeps the AT&T name on the building itself, a signal that the stadium's future, like its past, will continue to be shaped together.

"When it comes to connecting America's Team, there's only one choice: America's largest fiber network, backed by America's best guarantee," said AT&T Chairman & Chief Executive Officer John Stankey. "We deeply value our long and successful relationship with the Cowboys and look forward to continuing to innovate on behalf of fans to connect, share and stream effortlessly."

New for Cowboys Nation this SeasonAs part of the partnership, AT&T and the Cowboys are refreshing familiar fan favorites and introducing new experiences at AT&T Stadium this season, including:

  • Smarter Navigation: AT&T Stadium Wayfinding offers instant, no-download navigation from the parking lot to your seat, found through the Cowboys app and stadium kiosks.
  • More Immersive Experiences: Pose with the Pros brings an expanded AR photo experience with current players, Cowboys Legends and the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders. Reception Connection puts fans in a mixed reality catch-and-compete moment alongside Dak Prescott, and Connected Cam streams live fan video straight to the main videoboard.
  • AI-Powered Fan Engagement: The Starbase Connection Feature transforms fan-submitted photos into custom Cowboys hype videos across stadium boards.
  • Better Connectivity: AT&T Turbo Live gives every fan at AT&T Stadium, including customers of other carriers, reserved, high-priority network access to post, stream and share all game long.

As fan expectations continue to evolve, AT&T and the Cowboys will keep building the technology behind the next era of live sports and entertainment, one season, one game and one connection at a time.

1 Based on the number of fiber-to-the-home households using publicly available data.

About AT&T

We help more than 100 million U.S. families, friends and neighbors, plus nearly 2.5 million businesses, connect to greater possibility. From the first phone call 150+ years ago to our 5G wireless and multi-gig internet offerings today, we @ATT innovate to improve lives. For more information about AT&T Inc. (), please visit us at about.att.com. Investors can learn more at investors.att.com.

About AT&T Stadium

AT&T Stadium is the largest, most technologically advanced entertainment venue in the world. Designed by HKS and built by Manhattan Construction, the $1.2 billion stadium features two monumental arches, the world's largest HDTV video board cluster, an expansive retractable roof and the largest retractable end zone doors in the world. Features of the stadium include seating for 80,000 and expandability for up to 100,000, over 300 luxury suites, club seating on multiple levels and the Dallas Cowboys Pro Shop, open to the public year-round. Outside the stadium, the Miller Lite® House is a branded destination that boasts a 70-yard Cowboys turf field featuring field games, four video boards and over 60 television screens, two fantasy football screen walls and over 87,000 outdoor square-footage for event day experiences. The space also features two beer gardens and a walk-in beer cooler. The stadium is also home to a world-class collection of contemporary art, made up of over 100+ works of art by 66 established and emerging artists displayed on the walls and in the grand public spaces of the venue. In addition to being the home of the Dallas Cowboys since opening in 2009, the stadium has hosted FIFA World Cup 2026, the Grand Prix of Arlington, Super Bowl XLV, the 2010 NBA All Star Game, the annual Goodyear Cotton Bowl Classic, the annual Shriners Children's East-West Bowl, the 2014 NCAA Men's Final Four, the 2015 inaugural College Football Playoff Championship Game, the 2015 50th Anniversary Academy of Country Music Awards show and WrestleMania 32 & 38. data.title: Peru central bank lowers 2026 GDP growth estimate on El Niño impact
data.description:
By Marco Aquino

Peru's central bank lowered its projection for gross domestic product (GDP) growth this year to 3.2%, from a previous estimate of 3.4%, due to the impact of the El Niño weather phenomenon, central bank chief Julio Velarde said on Friday.

The bank also raised its 2026 inflation forecast to 4.2% from 3.8%, and projected 2027 GDP growth at 3.0%.

• In its quarterly report, the central bank projected the 2026 fiscal deficit at 1.5% of GDP, improved from a prior estimate of 1.8%, while projecting the 2027 fiscal deficit also at 1.5% of GDP.

• El Niño is already affecting Peru's fishing and agricultural sectors, posing a risk to exports of fishmeal and fruit - both strong growth drivers in recent years - even as the country remains the world's third-largest copper producer.

• Velarde said despite the current context, he sees "enormous potential" in Peru, mainly in the mining sector.

• He said an interest rate hike in coming months could not be ruled out, but he added the "opportune" moment would be sought to cut rates.

data.title: Duke Energy asks Carolinas customers to reduce electricity use during today's peak-demand period
data.description:
CHARLOTTE, N.C., Sept. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Unusually hot September weather is driving high electricity demand across parts of the Carolinas. Duke Energy is asking customers in North Carolina and South Carolina to voluntarily reduce electricity use from 2-8 p.m. today, Sept. 18, to help reduce demand on the power grid during the day's peak period.

Customers can help by taking simple steps during this peak period:

  • Raise your thermostat to the highest comfortable setting.
  • Avoid using major appliances such as washing machines, clothes dryers and dishwashers.
  • Limit use of electric ranges and ovens, which can add heat to your home and increase air conditioning demand.
  • Electric vehicle owners: Charge overnight, when demand is lower.

"Above-average heat puts pressure on the system during peak hours," said Kendal Bowman, president of Duke Energy's utility operations in North Carolina. "Small actions during the late afternoon and early evening can help reduce strain on the grid and support reliable service for everyone."

"We recognize it is inconvenient to reduce electric use, but it makes a real difference," said Tim Pearson, president of Duke Energy's utility operations in South Carolina. "We're using every available resource to meet demand so power keeps flowing to our communities."

Duke Energy has approximately 3.9 million electric customers in North Carolina and more than 870,000 electric customers in South Carolina.

Duke Energy

Duke Energy (), a Fortune 150 company headquartered in Charlotte, N.C., is one of America's largest energy holding companies. The company's electric utilities serve 8.7 million customers in North Carolina, South Carolina, Florida, Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky, and collectively own 55,700 megawatts of energy capacity. Its natural gas utilities serve 1.6 million customers in North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio and Kentucky.

Duke Energy is executing an energy modernization strategy, keeping customer value at the forefront as it invests in electric grid upgrades and efficient generation resources to strengthen the system and serve growing energy needs.

data.title: Bitcoin Trades Above $80,000 to Clock Third Day of Gains — Update
data.description:
By Joseph Wilkins and Kirk Maltais

Bitcoin rose for a third consecutive day, topping the $80,000 level that has been a stubborn cap in recent weeks.

The move higher comes after Thursday's session saw a tech-fueled relief rally with broad gains seen from chip makers to data-storage companies across the major indexes. This uptick is being seen in both major cryptocurrencies and in stocks for companies involved with blockchain technology.

The flagship cryptocurrency rose 5.9% at $80,966, solidifying a course for a positive end to the week after it had slipped to a near four-week low on the U.S. Senate's rejection of the Clarity Act on Tuesday.

Gains were not limited to major cryptocurrencies, with Coinbase Global climbing 11%, Strategy Inc. rising 13% and Circle Internet Group up 7%.

The Federal Reserve's quarter-point interest-rate hike Wednesday has complicated the path for nonyielding assets such as bitcoin and gold, which tend to lose their relative shine in a rate-raising cycle when compared with the return offered by bonds.

The rate hike is one reason fund traders posted net outflows for bitcoin exchange-traded funds for six out of seven prior trading sessions. Flows changed course Thursday, posting a net inflow of $159.5 million into those ETFs on Thursday, according to data from CoinGlass.

Bitcoin could outperform gold in the coming months if investors unwind some of the short positions surrounding cryptocurrency ETFs, according to JPMorgan.

Analysts led by JPMorgan's Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou wrote that short interest in the flagship bitcoin ETF--iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF, or IBIT--remains close to year-to-date highs, while short interest in gold ETFs stands below historical averages.

"This contrast suggests that bitcoin still faces an overall more skeptical positioning backdrop than gold, perhaps due to more elevated hedging demand, despite the recent inflows and build up of futures positioning," the analysts wrote.

Analysts are eyeing targets above the $80,000 mark should bitcoin continue its upward momentum. In a note published Friday, analysts with Coinbase Research said resistance targets above $80,0000 are $83,000, then $90,000, and then $95,000.

Should the rally lose steam and see bitcoin retreating back below $70,000, prices are expected to keep falling back to yearly lows around $58,000, said Coinbase in its note.

data.title: Week's Best: 'Finfluencers Are Rarely Qualified — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Barron's Advisor Staff

The internet is awash in videos created by self-styled financial influencers peddling investment strategies. Yet nearly all of them lack the qualifications considered necessary for providing financial advice, finds Legalaes, a financial licensing consultancy. The firm examined more than 1,700 posts that had been viewed more than 692 million times and determined that 29% were misleading. Just 2% of the social-media influencers were qualified to give financial advice, the firm found.

Among other most-read wealth management articles this week:

Morgan Stanley's 2027 pay grid. On Thursday, the Wall Street giant unveiled its 2027 advisor compensation plan, which follows the brokerage industry practice of using a grid to determine pay. Under Morgan Stanley's new compensation plan, the revenue thresholds for each of its 16 grid bands will increase by approximately 10%. That could shift some advisors into lower bands, reducing their payout percentages. Morgan Stanley is the first of the big four national brokerage firms to issue its annual compensation plan.

Schwab to pay up for crypto scam. An arbitration panel has ordered Charles Schwab to pay more than $1.3 million to resolve allegations that it failed to respond to red flags indicating an elderly client had fallen prey to a crypto scam. Swindlers apparently convinced the man, 82 at the time, that he owed money in connection with a refund they said he received in error and gained access to his computer, according to Scott Greco, the lawyer for the claimants. Schwab acknowledges the now-deceased client's losses but says it shouldn't have been responsible for reimbursing his sons.

New Jersey man charged in Ponzi scheme. The Securities and Exchange Commission accused Ernest Ossei Boateng and two New Jersey-based companies he controls of operating a $16 million Ponzi scheme, according to a civil complaint the regulator filed last week in a federal court in New York. The regulator says the affinity-fraud scam targeted inexperienced investors, many of whom are Christians of Ghanaian heritage in New York and New Jersey.

Veteran advisor's top lessons. Spuds Powell, a managing director at Kayne Anderson Rudnick, is ranked No. 3 in Barron's 2026 Top 100 Independent Advisors list and is a member of Barron's Hall of Fame. In a recent Barron's Advisor: The Way Forward podcast, he lists the most important lessons he's learned during his long career, including that "difficult" clients can help advisors grow and that lighthearted moments can build client relationships.

The real MVPs at wealth firms. In wealth management, team members who are technically in support roles can be the most instrumental to the success of a practice. They are essential for preventing mistakes, recognizing opportunities, and fostering client loyalty. For this week's Barron's Advisor Big Q, we asked team leaders to tell us about the significant contributions of employees who don't sit in the advisor chair.

data.title: Weil, Gotshal & Manges eyes merger options after rainmakers exit, Bloomberg News reports
data.description:
Law firm Weil, Gotshal & Manges is considering options for its future, including a potential merger with a competitor, Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

The company has been canvassing its partners and exploring ways to strengthen its business through strategic hires and promotions, and it could still remain independent, the report said.

Weil, Gotshal & Manges did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

This follows a string of departures at Weil, including prominent New York dealmaker Michael Aiello and five other M&A partners who are set to join Cravath, Swaine & Moore, along with two London-based M&A partners who recently moved to Sullivan & Cromwell.

Top leaders at the US law firm have become more open to the idea of combining with a competitor, and some have held informal discussions to gauge interest in a deal, the Bloomberg News report said.

Founded in 1931, Weil, Gotshal & Manges is a New York-based law firm known for its M&A, restructuring and bankruptcy practice, with about 1,200 lawyers worldwide.

data.title: Microsoft AI CEO: Recent OpenAI Incident is 'Pretty Serious Situation' — Market Talk
data.description: Recent AI security incidents disclosed by OpenAI are a cause for concern, Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman says on CNBC. "We don't know why that is or what's behind that, but that's a pretty serious situation." He praises OpenAI's disclosure of the incident but says it demonstrates the growing power and capability of leading AI models.(elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

data.title: US energy firms add rigs for second week to highest since May 2024, Baker Hughes says
data.description:
US energy firms this week added rigs for a second week in a row for the first time since July, energy services firm Baker Hughes said in its report on Friday.

The total oil and gas rig count, an early indicator of future output, rose by four to 595 in the week to September 18, its highest since May 2024. (BHGUSWTT), (BHGUSOILDRLW), (BHGUSGASDRLW) (USOIRC=ECI), (USGSRC=ECI)

Baker Hughes said this week's increase puts the total rig count up 53 rigs, or 10% above this time last year.

Baker Hughes said oil rigs rose by two to 452 this week, their highest since August, while gas rigs rose by two to 134, their highest since February 2026, and other miscellaneous rigs held at nine.

The oil and gas rig count declined by 7% in 2025, 5% in 2024, and 20% in 2023 as lower US oil prices prompted energy firms to focus more on boosting shareholder returns and paying down debt rather than increasing output.

But with spot US West Texas Intermediate crude prices expected to rise in 2026 for the first time in four years due to supply disruptions from the Iran war, the US Energy Information Administration projected that crude output will rise from a record 13.7 million barrels per day in 2025 to 13.8 million bpd in 2026.

On the gas side, EIA projected output will jump from a record 107.6 billion cubic feet per day in 2025 to 111.7 bcfd in 2026 as demand for the fuel rises to produce electricity for power-hungry data centers and liquefied natural gas for export.

data.title: Tata Steel gets court protection for ₹2,970 crore SDF payment till appeal disposal
data.description:
Global steel major Tata Steel Ltd on Friday (September 18) said the Calcutta High Court has disposed of an interim application filed by the company seeking an injunction on the Joint Plant Committee (JPC) utilising ₹2,970 crore deposited towards its Steel Development Fund (SDF) loan liability.

According to the court order dated September 17, 2026, which was received by Tata Steel on Friday, “till the appeal is disposed of, the fund shall not be utilised or disbursed to third parties.”

"As per the order of the Hon’ble High Court of Calcutta dated September 17, 2026, received by the Company today, i.e. September 18, 2026, Hon’ble High Court has disposed of the interim application with the direction that till the appeal is disposed of, the fund shall not be utilised or disbursed to third parties," according to a stock exchange filing.

The company had filed Interim Application GA/2/2026 before the Calcutta High Court seeking an injunction on the JPC utilising the ₹2,970 crore. The application was heard by the court on September 17.

Tata Steel paid ₹2,970 crore during FY2026

The development is related to Tata Steel's loan obligations arising from the SDF, which is managed by the JPC under the Ministry of Steel. Tata Steel had earlier sought a waiver of loans availed from the SDF, “in parity with SAIL”, or Steel Authority of India Ltd.

The company had filed a writ petition before the Calcutta High Court on April 2, 2024, against the rejection of its representation seeking the waiver. The matter was heard by the High Court over several hearings.

On May 24, 2024, the Single Bench of the Calcutta High Court dismissed Tata Steel's writ petition, while giving the company liberty to approach the JPC. Tata Steel subsequently sought further legal remedies and filed an appeal against the order before the Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court. The appeal is pending before the court.

On January 17, 2025, Tata Steel received a demand from the Ministry of Steel to make payment towards the outstanding balance of the SDF loan. During FY2026, the company discharged its liability towards the JPC aggregating to ₹2,970 crore, “without prejudice to its rights and contentions in the appeal,” Tata Steel said.

Tata Steel said its management believed that interim protection was necessary to safeguard the amount deposited by the company with the JPC. Accordingly, the company filed Interim Application GA/2/2026 before the Calcutta High Court seeking an injunction on the JPC utilising the ₹2,970 crore.

The interim application was heard on September 17, 2026. The High Court subsequently disposed of the application and directed that the fund should not be utilised or disbursed to third parties until the appeal is disposed of.

Shares of Tata Steel Ltd ended at ₹184.75, down by ₹3.25, or 1.73%, on the BSE.

data.title: Fitch Raises Thailand's Outlook to Stable — Market Talk
data.description: Fitch Ratings raises its outlook on Thailand to stable, citing increased confidence in the government's debt/GDP ratio over the medium term. When Fitch revised Thailand's outlook to negative last September, it forecast general government debt to stabilize at just below 65% of GDP. Fitch now says it expects general government debt to stabilize by fiscal year 2028, which starts in October of next year, at just below 63%. Thailand's current coalition government seems to have a stronger grip on power than its recent predecessors, Fitch says. The country's Long-Term Foreign and Local-Currency Issuer Default Ratings were affirmed at BBB+. (stephen.nakrosis@wsj.com)

data.title: Volkswagen Slashes Guidance as Woes Pile Up — Update
data.description:
By Andrea Figueras and Mauro Orru

Volkswagen said it was cutting a key profitability target for the year as it scrambles to contain the fallout from a host of challenges that forced it to significantly downsize its workforce.

The beleaguered German carmaker said Friday that it expected an operating return on sales of up to 1% this year, down from a prior estimate between 4% and 5.5%. The new projection, announced just before market close in Germany, is below analysts' forecast of 4.1%, sending Volkswagen shares nearly 5.6% lower.

The guidance revision comes weeks after Volkswagen's supervisory board approved a plan to double job cuts to 100,000, arguing the group has to remain competitive at a time when the auto sector struggles with U.S. tariffs, rising manufacturing costs and stiff competition from Chinese rivals.

Earlier this month, Volkswagen said it was selling its factory in the German city of Osnabrueck to Israel's Aurelius Capital and the state of Lower Saxony, which aim to repurpose the site to make defense equipment.

The group said restructuring expenses from early retirement packages for some employees as well as the planned sale in Osnabrueck had forced it to revise the outlook.

Long considered a fixture of Germany's industrial base, Volkswagen has been seeking to revive its fortunes for years now, but challenges keep piling up.

The company said a further deterioration, especially in the Chinese market, as well as a shift in demand for battery-electric vehicles, would weigh on operating earnings, meaning that performance would fall short of original expectations, particularly for the Audi and Volkswagen Passenger Cars brands.

The group also said the revision was due, in part, to a non-cash impairment of goodwill of roughly 6 billion euros, equivalent to $6.89 billion, in relation to Porsche AG, in which Volkswagen commands a stake of more than 75%.

Porsche AG has been grappling with its own challenges, and Volkswagen said the impairment would harm its own operating profit in the third quarter.

The sports-car maker is also moving to lower costs, including cutting 5,000 jobs, as it struggles with a decline in demand from Chinese consumers for high-end imported cars.

Volkswagen said it expected a hit of around 2 billion euros in the second half of the year due to restructuring costs, the deteriorating environment and the impairment.

Revenue for the year should decline to around 315 billion euros from 321.9 billion euros in 2025. It had previously said that sales could be stable or decrease by up to 3%, but the new figure is broadly equivalent to the midpoint of a prior guidance range.

Meanwhile, it said it continued to expect net cash flow at its automotive division between 3 billion euros and 6 billion euros and net liquidity in the segment between 32 billion euros and 34 billion euros.

Volkswagen said its outlook was based on assumption that tariffs would remain unchanged and noted that those estimates didn't take into account possible future effects from the war in the Middle East.

The company plans to publish its first-half report on Oct. 29.

data.title: Global Bond Yields Rise Amid Expectations of More Rate Rises — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Miriam Mukuru and Emese Bartha

Global bond yields rose on Friday, hovering near multiyear highs, after the Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan raised interest rates this week, with more increases expected to come.

The Fed raised interest rates by a quarter point on Wednesday, and signaled another raise to come this year, which convinced markets about the seriousness of the Fed's inflation fight.

This initially pulled yields away from recent highs. However, the factors that drove bond yields higher in the first place remained, namely the risk of oil prices staying elevated for a prolonged period, high debt levels, and competition for funding from AI-related companies.

"The Fed may have reinforced its inflation-fighting credentials, but heavy government borrowing, elevated term premium and growing private-sector competition for capital mean long yields remain supported by forces that monetary policy alone cannot easily resolve," said Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com.

The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield rose back to the 5% level reached earlier this week for the first time since 2023. It was recently at 5.002%. The two-year yield, which tracks Fed moves more closely, touched 4.744%, its highest intraday yield since July 2024 when it hit 4.775%.

Yield moves have mirrored oil prices in recent weeks, but the trend broke on Friday, as Brent fell 1% to $104 a barrel.

Following a Bank of England's hold on Thursday, the Bank of Japan raised its policy rate to 1.25% on Friday, the highest since 1995, albeit in a split vote.

The 10-year Japanese government bond yield was steady at 2.998% after the BOJ decision. With two board members voting against the rate increase, the move wasn't enough to boost the yen, which weakened nearly 1% against the dollar.

Analysts warned that global yields could still rise further.

"The global rebuilding of term premia is not yet complete, and markets still have scope to price a more aggressive path of central bank rate hikes," Societe Generale rates strategists said in a note.

The 10-year German Bund yield rose 2.0 basis points to 3.500%, below a peak of 3.572% hit earlier this week, its highest since 2009. The 10-year U.K. gilt yield climbed 5.7 bps to 5.275%, below this week's peak of 5.493%, its highest since 2007.

Central bank leaders acknowledged the rising inflation risks and signaled more rate rises in the coming months, causing markets to price in three or more rate increases by major central banks in the next year, LSEG data showed.

"The medicine from the Fed is working and may have prevented the rates selloff from spiraling out of control," said Commerzbank rates strategist Marco Stoeckle in a note.

Gilt yields were also lifted after Friday's U.K. retail sales data for August came in better than expected, suggesting that household spending stayed resilient despite high energy costs and increased prospects of higher interest rates by the Bank of England in the future.

  • Paulo Trevisani contributed to this article.

Write to Miriam Mukuru at miriam.mukuru@wsj.com and Emese Bartha at emese.bartha@wsj.com
